abstract: In this paper the applicability of magnetron sputtered Ge-Sb-V/TiSi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> thermocouples in thermal converter construction has been analysed and described. Testing device with linear symmetry was prepared on 10times10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> D263 Schott foil glass substrates 7 mum thick. The converter contained the MoSi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> heater and the integrated thermopile based on 2times6 "hot" and "cold" junctions of silicide/semiconductor type. The Ge-Sb-V alloy with various content of V was examined. Thermal sensitivity of thermocouples was varied from 160 to 224 muV/K. The performance of these converters in ambient temperature range of 300-773 K under normal pressure has been evaluated and reported

articleTitle: The development of the conductive phase in some thick-film resistors during firing
publicationTitle: 28th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology: Meeting the Challenges of Electronics Technology Progress, 2005.
abstract: The development of the conductive phase in some thick-film resistors with both low and with high temperature coefficients of resistivity was studied using X-ray diffraction analysis and electron microscopy. After long-term high-temperature firing the conductive phase in thick-film resistors based on RuO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> remains unchanged, while the ruthenates decompose. This is presumably due to interactions of the ruthenate with the silica-rich glass phase in the resistors. The reaction kinetics is faster for higher concentrations of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>

articleTitle: Use of the dynamic heterogeneities for creation of temporary operating conductive tracks
publicationTitle: 28th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology: Meeting the Challenges of Electronics Technology Progress, 2005.
abstract: Creation of conductive tracks between contact points in the form of dynamic heterogeneities (heightened concentration of the charge carrier in the sphere attached to the surface that is the equivalent to metallized track only at the moment of signal transmission) is proposed. Such tracks are created owing to internal photo-effect with irradiation of sufficient intensity (laser or other kind) of the section between contact points at the efficiently appointed moment

articleTitle: Best quality strategy for electronics production
publicationTitle: 28th International Spring Seminar on Electronics Technology: Meeting the Challenges of Electronics Technology Progress, 2005.
abstract: In the last years the authors developed new and powerful quality cost models to optimize quality strategies in electronics production. These models are successful in use and were published in some books, tutorials, articles (see [Martin Oppermann (2002)], [Martin Oppermann, Wilfried Sauer and Heinz Wohlrabe (2003)] and [Martin Oppermann, Wilfried Sauer, Heinz Wohlrabe and Thomas Zerna (2003)]) and presentations at important conferences like ECTC, ISSE and SMT hybrid packaging. These models look for the quality process only to find out the optimized quality strategy by the minimum of costs. The next step was the development of an extension of these models to include the production process and its quality dependent properties into the cost models. The question is: how influences the improvement of a production process by investment the quality and the costs of the products? How much time does it need to reach a better quality level by lower costs? The new extension of the quality cost models gives help to the production engineers to make a decision about the right quality strategy
